co_lost_wall_the.blurb: A west-facing quartzite crag perched high above Vallecito Creek, part of the Vallecito Crags near Durango. Fourteen routes, most of them bolted, plus a few trad lines including a couple of moderate two-pitch outings. The grades skew hard: one route around 5.9, a handful at 5.10, and nine at 5.12, so this is more a place for strong sport climbers than for beginners. The stone is thin and technical, with slabby faces and some roofs near the tops of the lines. It sits at roughly 8,600 feet and stays cool in summer, with a secluded, alpine feel typical of the whole Vallecito zone, where quartzite can be flaky and route-finding takes care.

co_main_wall_15.blurb: The principal sector of the Halidome, a huge granite face above Empire at roughly 10,000 feet. Most of the fourteen routes are long alpine-style lines, with just a couple of sport climbs, and the difficulty is steep: a single 5.9, one 5.10, three 5.11s, eight at 5.12 and one 5.13. Many are multi-pitch and big-wall in feel, with sharp edges that can chew a rope, and the setting brings real mountain weather even on bolted climbs. Routes are located relative to a tall free-standing pillar and a sloping ledge partway up the face, reached by a steep boulder-filled gully and a ramp along the base. Best for fit, experienced parties who want long hard days.

co_pleasure_dome.blurb: A small, sunny, secluded granite wall near Buena Vista, about 50 feet tall, that is mostly bolted sport climbing with a single trad line. Of fourteen routes, the bulk sit in the 5.11 range (seven), with a few at 5.10 and 5.12 and one easier 5.8 for warming up. The rock faces away from the trail, so the wall is not obvious until you are on it. Across the valley, a separate cliff has top-rope options. A good pick for intermediate-to-strong sport climbers who want a quiet, short-route day in a valley known for solid granite and bolted face climbs.

co_main_amphitheater.blurb: The showpiece sector of Cougar, a sustained cliff reached by a long uphill walk near Steamboat Springs, at about 8,450 feet. Fourteen routes mix nine sport lines and five trad lines, with the difficulty centred on 5.10 (seven routes) and a few stretching to 5.11 and 5.12. The easiest trad and mixed climbs are the way to go for those below 5.10, since the bolted routes are largely 5.10a or harder. Features include a prominent pillar, a roof and good cracks. Expect long, concentrated climbing in the afternoon sun; it is a rewarding but committing day for climbers comfortable with the grade.

co_outrageous_overhang.blurb: A steep, shady granite wall on Independence Pass, the first crag you meet when walking in from the road, only a short uphill hike away. Mostly bolted sport lines (thirteen of fourteen routes) with one trad line, and the grades cluster at 5.12, seven of them, with a couple at 5.11, a 5.13, and a few easier ones from 5.6 to 5.9. There is little in the way of warm-ups, so it suits climbers working mid to low 5.12 who like power and steepness. The rock is clean and the lines well bolted; a 60 metre rope handles nearly everything. High elevation means cool air and afternoon storms.

co_checkerboard_rock.blurb: A granite crag of roughly 200 feet on Lumpy Ridge, just below Batman Rock, above Estes Park. All fourteen routes are trad, spread across 5.8 to 5.11 with the heaviest numbers at 5.9 and 5.10. A chimney splits the face and a ledge crosses it high up; the angle is a little less than vertical, so even the cracks feel slabby, and the protection can be thin and the flares insecure in classic Lumpy style. Most routes are one or two pitches, which makes it a handy half-day choice, though the walk in takes the better part of an hour and the rock is tough to spot through trees.

_expect.name: Subterranean Wall (A.K.A.) The Dragon's Den, The

co_subterranean_wall_a_k_a_the_dragon_s_.blurb: A small, quiet bouldering wall tucked into the trees of Alderfer/Three Sisters Park near Evergreen. Fourteen problems, mostly ten to twenty-five feet tall, so good spotters and a confident head help. The range is wide for so few problems: a handful of V0 to V2 lines, a middle group around V4 to V7, and a couple of hard test-pieces at V9 and V10. Many lines and traverses are possible. The wall catches sun most of the day, which makes it a pleasant spring or fall stop, and it is secluded and a little hard to find, so expect to search a bit for the rock band above the trail.
